“This is how I want my daughter to be.”

“Castle Rock” (2018-2019) is a psychological horror anthology that weaves together the settings, characters, and themes of the Stephen King canon into a brand-new saga. Set in the cursed Maine town that gives the show its name, the series explores the “darkness and light” hidden within its woods.

Season 1 follows a death row attorney (André Holland) investigating a mysterious, ageless prisoner (Bill Skarsgård) found in the depths of Shawshank Prison.

Season 2 shifts gears into a psychological origin story for Annie Wilkes from Misery (Lizzy Caplan). It’s an atmospheric, slow-burning tribute to King’s legendary storytelling, exploring how a place can be haunted as much by its history as by its monsters.

source_details.synopsis: Castle Rock is an American supernatural horror television series, adapted from Stephen King's fictional town of Castle Rock, Maine. The series was created by Sam Shaw and Dustin Thomason, and premiered on Hulu on July 25, 2018. The first season starred André Holland, Melanie Lynskey, Bill Skarsgård, Jane Levy, and Sissy Spacek. A second season acting as a separate stand-alone story premiered on October 23, 2019, starring Lizzy Caplan, Paul Sparks, Barkhad Abdi, Yusra Warsama, Elsie Fisher, Matthew Alan, and Tim Robbins. In November 2020, Hulu cancelled the series after two seasons.
